descriptionChirho: A Hebrew adverb (מָחָר) meaning 'tomorrow, the next day', used both independently and with the preposition le- ('for tomorrow'). Found frequently in narrative contexts indicating the following day (e.g., Exod 8:19; 9:5; 1 Sam 11:9-10; Josh 11:6). Multilingual evidence is consistent across all forms: eng 'tomorrow/for-tomorrow', spa 'manana/para-manana', arb 'غَدًا/لِغَدٍ', kor '내일/내일을-위하여', swa 'kesho/kwa-kesho', hin 'कल/कल-के-लिए'. The prepositional form le-machar (S110961) is the same temporal adverb with a grammatical preposition, not a separate sense.
